id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::MGM Resorts International
financial_impact: MGM disclosed an estimated ~$100 million negative impact to Adjusted Property EBITDAR for Las Vegas Strip and Regional Operations, plus under $10 million in one-time remediation/legal/incident-response costs; company said it expected to be largely covered by cyber insurance. A related shareholder/consumer class-action settlement was reached in 2025.
ransom: MGM has stated it did not pay a ransom (unlike sister-incident Caesars); no confirmed dollar figure for a demand specific to MGM has been publicly disclosed.
downtime: Core systems (slot machines, digital key cards, reservations, payment processing) were down for approximately 10 days before full restoration.
data_impact: Personal information (names, contact details, driver's license/SSN/passport numbers for some) of roughly 37 million MGM Rewards members was compromised.
summary: Scattered Spider used a vishing/social-engineering attack against MGM's IT help desk to obtain credentials, then deployed ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware, forcing MGM to shut down casino floor systems, digital hotel room keys, slot machines, ATMs, restaurant/payment systems and websites across 30+ properties for roughly 10 days.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Caesars Entertainment
financial_impact: Caesars disclosed the incident in an SEC 8-K; ongoing consumer class-action litigation (Caesars Entertainment Data Breach Litigation). Specific total incident cost beyond the ransom payment not publicly broken out.
ransom: Attackers initially demanded $30 million; Caesars paid approximately $15 million in cryptocurrency. The FBI later tracked and froze a portion of the payment as it moved through crypto exchanges.
downtime: Caesars stated its hotel, casino and online operations were not significantly disrupted (unlike MGM); recovery was largely on the data-breach/notification track rather than an operational-outage track.
data_impact: Loyalty program database of more than 65 million Caesars Rewards members exposed, including driver's license and Social Security numbers for a subset of members.
summary: Attackers compromised a third-party IT support vendor via social engineering to breach Caesars' network and exfiltrate the ~6TB Caesars Rewards loyalty database before Caesars negotiated and paid a ransom; the attack occurred just before, and is closely associated with, the MGM incident by the same threat-actor ecosystem.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Carnival Corporation & plc
date: April 2026 (initial access April 14; discovered/blocked April 22; disclosed publicly ~mid-May 2026)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed as a specific dollar figure by Carnival; the company began offering two years of complimentary TransUnion credit monitoring to affected US residents, an ongoing cost. Litigation/regulatory exposure likely given the scale of records.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed; ShinyHunters is an extortion-focused (data-theft, not necessarily encryption) group and threatened to publish/sell the data if terms were not met.
downtime: No major operational/cruise-booking outage reported; this was primarily a data-theft/social-engineering incident rather than an encryption/downtime event.
data_impact: Data breach notice filed in Maine listed 5,995,277 affected individuals; ShinyHunters claimed 8.7 million records stolen. Exposed data included names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, dates of birth, and government ID numbers (driver's license, passport).
summary: ShinyHunters used social engineering to trick a Carnival employee into granting IT system access, then used the compromised account to copy personal data from a limited portion of Carnival's systems before being blocked; the gang later claimed 8.7 million stolen records and published data on its leak site.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Compass Group Australia (Sydney-based catering/support services group)
victim: Compass Group Australia (Sydney-based catering/support services group)
date: September 2024 (first attack disclosed Sept 4; second Medusa-affiliate attack later in September, data posted Sept 18, 2024)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed by Compass Group; company activated its incident response plan and notified employees, clients, suppliers and regulators.
ransom: First attack: Medusa demanded US$2 million to delete/not publish the ~785.5GB of stolen data (with a US$100,000/day deadline-extension fee). Second (separate) attack: ransom demanded was US$100,000. Not publicly confirmed whether any payment was made.
downtime: Specific downtime duration not publicly detailed in press coverage; company stated it secured systems and launched an investigation with external cybersecurity specialists.
data_impact: Near 1TB combined across both incidents; data included employee wage declarations and scanned passports/driver's licenses of contractors and staff, with the threat actor threatening publication on its dark-web leak site.
summary: Medusa ransomware affiliates breached Compass Group's Australian IT network twice within the same month, exfiltrating close to 1TB of data combined, including employee wage records and scanned passports/driver's licenses of contractors, then threatened publication on Medusa's leak site.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Panera Bread
date: March 2024 (outage began March 22, resolved around March 26, 2024)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed by Panera; the company did not release financial figures. Independent security analysts estimated such multi-day enterprise ransomware disruptions typically cost tens of millions of dollars in lost sales and recovery, but no Panera-specific figure has been confirmed.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed; no group claimed responsibility and Panera did not comment on any ransom demand or payment.
downtime: Approximately one week (March 22-26, 2024) of major IT outage across point-of-sale, online ordering, loyalty and phone systems before restoration.
data_impact: A subsequent notice confirmed an employee data breach tied to the March incident (SSNs and other employee personal data); customer payment-data exposure was not confirmed.
summary: A ransomware attack encrypted numerous Panera Bread virtual machines, taking down point-of-sale systems, online/mobile ordering, the loyalty (MyPanera) program, and internal phone systems across the chain's roughly 2,160 cafés; stores stayed open but had to fall back to cash-only transactions during the outage.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Nordic Choice Hotels
country: Norway/Scandinavia (200 properties across Scandinavia, Finland, and the Baltics)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed as a specific dollar figure.
ransom: Nordic Choice stated it deliberately did not contact Conti and had not received (or did not intend to pay) a ransom demand; no payment reported.
downtime: Replacement/workaround solutions were in place at most hotels within days of the attack (over the following weekend), with normal operations restored within about a week.
data_impact: Guest booking data and Nordic Choice Club (loyalty) member data were confirmed potentially exposed; no indication passwords or payment card data were affected.
summary: Conti ransomware hit Nordic Choice Hotels' central IT systems, disabling reservation, check-in/check-out, room key-card and payment systems across its ~200-property, 16,000-employee hotel network; staff fell back to manual processes while replacement systems were rolled out property-by-property.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Rivers Casino Des Plaines / Rush Street Gaming
victim: Rivers Casino Des Plaines / Rush Street Gaming
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; the casino faced a class-action lawsuit over the data breach.
ransom: For the 2025 Rivers Casino Philadelphia/Rush Street Gaming Cicada3301 claim, an undisclosed ransom was demanded with a stated deadline (Feb 15, 2025); no payment publicly confirmed. No ransom figure disclosed for the 2023 Illinois breach.
downtime: No major operational outage publicly reported; this was primarily a data-theft/notification incident rather than an encryption/downtime event.
data_impact: Names, birth dates, contact info, driver's license/government ID numbers, Social Security numbers, bank account and tax ID information, and passport numbers for a subset of customers and employees (at least 8,151 individuals per Comparitech); the 2025 Cicada3301 claim alleged 2.56TB of data stolen from Rush Street Gaming.
summary: Hackers accessed files containing personal data of customers and employees at Rivers Casino (Illinois); the breach was discovered months after the intrusion, leading to consumer notification, class-action litigation, and a separate 2025 Cicada3301 extortion claim against the related Rivers Casino Philadelphia/Rush Street Gaming entity.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Disneyland Paris
date: June 2025 (claimed on leak site June 20, 2025; group teased on social media June 12)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; Disneyland Paris had not acknowledged the breach in public statements found.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed/unclear whether a ransom was demanded of Disneyland Paris directly versus its partner firm.
downtime: No park operational disruption reported; this was a third-party/supply-chain data-exposure incident rather than an IT outage at the park itself.
data_impact: Approximately 64GB / ~39,000 files of construction and renovation-related documents and media allegedly exposed via a Disneyland partner company, not confirmed to include guest personal data.
summary: Anubis ransomware claimed the largest data leak in Disneyland Paris's history, alleging the data (obtained via breach of a construction/renovation partner company rather than Disneyland directly) included ~39,000 files of park construction and renovation plans, exposing images/videos of attraction designs (Crush's Coaster, Frozen, Ratatouille, Buzz Lightyear, Phantom Manor, etc.). Disneyland Paris had not publicly confirmed the claims as of the reporting.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Inspired Entertainment, Inc.
downtime: The affected IT systems have now been substantially restored to full operational capabilities.
data_impact: Company data, including personal data, was exfiltrated.
summary: On November 8, 2023, Inspired Entertainment, Inc. detected a ransomware attack that disrupted its corporate IT systems. The company initiated response protocols and engaged cybersecurity experts, later discovering that personal data had been exfiltrated on November 15, 2023.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Yum! Brands, Inc.
downtime: Less than 300 restaurants in the United Kingdom were closed for one day; all stores are now operational and systems are expected to be largely restored in the coming days.
data_impact: Data was taken from the Company's network; no evidence that customer databases were stolen.
summary: On January 18, 2023, Yum! Brands, Inc. announced a ransomware attack that impacted certain information technology systems. The company initiated response protocols and engaged cybersecurity professionals, while confirming that less than 300 restaurants in the UK were temporarily closed but are now operational.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::England Hockey
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 129GB of data stolen
summary: England Hockey is investigating a potential data breach after the AiLock ransomware gang listed it as a victim on its data leak site. The threat actor allegedly stole 129GB of data and threatened to publish the files unless a ransom is paid. The organization is prioritizing an inquiry with both internal teams and external experts to understand the situation.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Washington Hotel
downtime: The incident is impacting operations at some Washington Hotel brand properties, including the temporary unavailability of credit card terminals. The firm says it recorded no significant operational disruption.
data_impact: various business data; customer data is unlikely to be exposed
summary: Washington Hotel in Japan disclosed a ransomware infection incident that compromised its servers, exposing various business data. The hotel brand has engaged cybersecurity experts and is assessing the impact while confirming that customer data is likely safe due to separate storage. The attack occurred on February 13, 2026, and has temporarily affected operations at some properties.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Toronto Zoo
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: impacted individuals' names, street address information, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, last four digits of credit card numbers, associated expiration dates
summary: The Toronto Zoo experienced a ransomware attack in January 2024, resulting in a data breach that exposed personal and financial information of employees, volunteers, and donors. The Akira ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack and published the stolen data on their dark web site, which included sensitive information from transactions dating back to 2000.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Krispy Kreme
downtime: Krispy Kreme experienced operational disruptions, particularly with online ordering, and took measures to contain and remediate the breach.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Play ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on Krispy Kreme, impacting its business operations and online ordering system. The gang alleged that they stole sensitive data from the company's network and threatened to publish it unless a ransom was paid.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Bologna Football Club 1909
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Bologna FC confirmed a ransomware attack by the RansomHub group, which resulted in the theft and online publication of sensitive data. The leaked data includes personal and confidential information of players, financial records, and medical records, among other details.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Grand Palais Rmn
downtime: operational disruptions were reported, but a solution allowed stores and boutiques to operate autonomously
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Grand Palais Rmn in France suffered a cyberattack during the Olympic Games, which was identified as a ransomware attack. Although operational disruptions occurred, the museums under its management continued to operate normally, and there were no signs of data exfiltration, despite a ransom note being left by the attackers demanding payment in cryptocurrency.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Christie's
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: at least 500,000 clients' full names, addresses, ID document details, and various other sensitive personal information
summary: Christie's, a British auction house, notified clients of a data breach involving the RansomHub ransomware gang, which accessed and extracted customer files between May 8 and May 9, 2024. The auction house is offering affected individuals a free twelve-month subscription to an identity theft monitoring service and has taken steps to secure its systems following the incident.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Omni Hotels
downtime: Certain systems were brought offline, most of which have been restored. Omni quickly launched an investigation with a leading cybersecurity response team, which is ongoing.
data_impact: 3,539,089 records of Omni Hotels visitors with sensitive information, including names, email addresses, and mailing addresses.
summary: The Daixin ransomware gang claimed a cyberattack on Omni Hotels, threatening to publish sensitive customer information unless a ransom is paid. The attack caused a nationwide IT outage affecting various systems, and the gang has claimed to have stolen over 3.5 million visitor records.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Omni Hotels Resorts
downtime: Systems are being manually restored from scratch, with some systems expected to be available again on Thursday.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Omni Hotels Resorts confirmed a cyberattack caused a nationwide IT outage affecting its locations. The hotel chain is currently restoring encrypted servers from backups and has taken down impacted systems to protect its data.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Gallery Systems
downtime: Systems taken offline to prevent further encryption; working to restore access with last available backup.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Gallery Systems, a software solutions provider for museums, suffered a ransomware attack on December 28, 2023, leading to significant IT outages. The attack encrypted certain computer systems, preventing them from operating, and the company is working to restore access while notifying law enforcement and conducting an internal investigation.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Gellyberry Studios
downtime: Server availability returned late on Friday; developers are manually restoring affected accounts and data.
data_impact: 17,000 player accounts affected; in-game items and progress lost.
summary: Gellyberry Studios, the indie game developer of 'Ethyrial: Echoes of Yore,' suffered a ransomware attack that encrypted all data on their main server, including local backups, resulting in the loss of 17,000 player accounts. The developers opted not to pay the ransom, fearing that it would not guarantee the return of their data, and are instead working to manually restore the lost accounts and items.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::LDLC ASVEL
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 32 GB of data stolen, including personal data of players, passports, ID cards, financial, taxation, and legal documents, NDAs, contracts, and confidential letters
summary: LDLC ASVEL, a French professional basketball team, confirmed a data breach following a ransomware attack by the NoEscape gang. The attackers claimed to have stolen 32 GB of sensitive data and are threatening to publish it unless a ransom is negotiated. The club is currently assessing the impact of the breach and has reported the incident to the national data protection authority.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Motel One
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 150 credit cards, customer addresses, booking confirmations for the past 3 years
summary: Motel One was targeted by the BlackCat/ALPHV ransomware gang, which claimed to have stolen nearly 24.5 million files, including sensitive customer data. The hotel chain reported that while the attackers infiltrated their network, the impact was minimized due to effective protective measures. However, the threat actors have threatened to leak the stolen data if a ransom is not negotiated within five days.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Gaijin Entertainment
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: A ransomware operation has targeted Russian players of the Enlisted multiplayer first-person shooter by distributing trojanized versions of the game through a fake website. The ransomware, which mimics the notorious WannaCry, encrypts files and demands a ransom from victims within three days.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Crown Resorts
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Crown Resorts confirmed it suffered a data breach after its GoAnywhere secure file-sharing server was compromised by the Clop ransomware gang. The gang is extorting Crown Resorts, claiming to have stolen data from its networks, although the company states there is no evidence of customer data being compromised.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::H-Hotels
downtime: communication outages
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Play ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyber attack on H-Hotels, resulting in communication outages for the company. The attack involved the use of ransomware to encrypt devices on the network after gaining access through vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::New York Racing Association
downtime: NYRA's website remains out of reach, but core operations were not interrupted.
data_impact: personally identifiable information of NYRA employees and their beneficiaries
summary: The Hive ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyber attack on the New York Racing Association (NYRA) on June 30, 2022, which compromised member data. The attack did not affect day-to-day racing operations, but the association's website faced accessibility issues, and the hackers published a link to download stolen files.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::San Francisco 49ers
downtime: The 49ers are still restoring systems, indicating that the breached devices were likely encrypted.
data_impact: 20,930 individuals affected; personal information including names and Social Security numbers.
summary: The San Francisco 49ers experienced a data breach due to a ransomware attack by the Blackbyte gang, affecting over 20,000 individuals. The attackers accessed and stole personal information, and the team is working on restoring their systems while enhancing security protocols.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::hotel and spa in Oregon
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 1,534 employees affected; sensitive information including names, Social Security Numbers, date of birth, phone numbers, and email addresses
summary: The ALPHV ransomware gang has launched a dedicated website allowing employees and customers of a hotel and spa in Oregon to check if their data was stolen during a ransomware attack. They claim to have stolen 112GB of data, including sensitive employee information for 1,534 individuals, and are using this site to pressure the hotel into paying a ransom to prevent public exposure of the data.

id: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment::Roblox
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: A new ransomware named 'WannaFriendMe' has been discovered, which sells its decryptor on the Roblox platform using in-game currency. This ransomware variant, related to Chaos ransomware, encrypts files and demands payment in Robux for decryption, targeting young gamers. Roblox has since removed the Game Pass and the account responsible for selling the decryptor.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::JBS S.A. / JBS USA
financial_impact: Direct operational disruption to global meat supply; JBS did not publicly quantify total losses beyond the ransom. Widely cited as one of the most consequential critical-infrastructure attacks of 2021.
ransom: REvil initially demanded $22.5 million; JBS negotiated and paid $11 million in Bitcoin.
downtime: Multiple North American and Australian plants shut for roughly a day-plus; JBS said the majority of facilities were operational again within days, choosing to pay to avoid prolonged disruption and possible data exfiltration.
data_impact: JBS said it paid partly to ensure no data was exfiltrated; no large-scale data leak was confirmed at the time.
summary: The world's largest meat processor was hit by REvil, forcing shutdown of beef and pork slaughterhouses across the US, Canada and Australia and disrupting roughly a fifth of US meat capacity. Internal DHS records later characterized JBS's pre-attack cybersecurity as unusually poor. Ransomware.live also tracks a later 2026 'coinbasecartel' posting recycling ~3TB of JBS data, illustrating re-extortion.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI)
financial_impact: Estimated $350–$400 million reduction in fiscal-2025 net sales; net income impact of $50–$60 million and adjusted EBITDA impact of ~$40–$50 million. Included ~$20 million in manual-workaround costs and ~$5 million in remediation. Company said it expects insurance proceeds to be adequate to substantially offset losses.
downtime: Systems taken offline in early June 2025; company ran manual workarounds and said the operational impact was mostly contained to the quarter, with phased restoration over subsequent weeks.
data_impact: Not detailed publicly; impact framed primarily as operational/supply disruption.
summary: North America's largest grocery distributor and primary supplier to Whole Foods was forced to take core systems offline after a June 2025 cyberattack, crippling electronic ordering and invoicing across its 53 distribution centers serving 30,000+ retail locations and emptying shelves nationwide. One of the largest quantified financial hits in the sector.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::Dole plc (Dole Food Company)
financial_impact: Total incident impact of $10.5 million for the quarter ended March 31, 2023 (of which $4.8 million related to continuing operations); CEO warned the financial impact would not be fully recoverable through insurance.
downtime: North American operations briefly shut down; most disruptive to Fresh Vegetables and Chilean businesses. All impacted servers and end-user computers were subsequently restored or rebuilt with third-party IR support.
data_impact: Dole later disclosed the attack breached data of almost 3,900 US workers.
summary: One of the world's largest fresh-produce suppliers suffered a February 2023 ransomware attack that hit about half of Legacy Dole's servers and a quarter of end-user computers, briefly shutting North American operations and causing widely reported packaged-salad shortages on US store shelves.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::Ahold Delhaize USA (Giant Food, Hannaford, Food Lion, Stop & Shop, The Giant Company)
victim: Ahold Delhaize USA (Giant Food, Hannaford, Food Lion, Stop & Shop, The Giant Company)
financial_impact: Not separately quantified in dollar terms publicly; costs include breach response and two years of free credit monitoring/identity protection for 2.24M affected individuals.
ransom: No ransom reported paid — attackers published ~800GB of data on their leak site, indicating non-payment.
downtime: Network issues across US pharmacies and supermarkets in November 2024; systems restored over following weeks.
data_impact: Breach affected 2,242,521 people; leaked data included names, postal/email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and government IDs (SSNs, driver's licenses, passports).
summary: The US division of the multinational grocery/food retailer detected unauthorized access on Nov 6, 2024, disrupting pharmacies and supermarket network systems. INC Ransom claimed the attack in April 2025, asserting up to 6TB of stolen data; the incident became one of the largest food-retail data breaches on record.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::NEW Cooperative Inc.
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; the co-op proactively took systems offline to contain impact rather than pay.
ransom: BlackMatter demanded $5.9 million, escalating to $11.8 million if unpaid within five days. Reporting indicated the co-op did not pay.
downtime: Systems taken offline proactively to contain the threat; operations managed via workarounds while remediation proceeded with law enforcement and security experts.
data_impact: BlackMatter claimed theft of financial information, HR data, R&D information and source code for the 'SoilMap' agricultural technology platform.
summary: An Iowa farm cooperative providing feed, grain and crop-protection services was hit by BlackMatter, which locked systems used to manage food supply chains and animal-feeding schedules. The co-op said ~40% of US grain production runs through its software and warned the attack could 'break the supply chain very shortly,' making it a landmark food-security incident.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::KP Snacks
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; disruption to order processing and distribution for roughly two months with supply-chain knock-on to retailers.
ransom: Conti operated double-extortion with a leak-site countdown; ransom amount and any payment not publicly confirmed.
downtime: Order placement and delivery disrupted from late January with no normal service expected until at least end of March 2022.
data_impact: Conti published samples including credit-card statements, birth certificates, and spreadsheets with employee addresses and phone numbers on its leak site.
summary: The UK snack maker (Hula Hoops, McCoy's, KP Nuts, Tyrrells, Butterkist) discovered a Conti ransomware attack on Jan 28, 2022 that disrupted IT systems so severely it could not safely process orders or dispatch goods, prompting warnings of crisp and snack shortages through at least March.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::Maple Leaf Foods
financial_impact: Company acknowledged the outage would cause operational and financial impact and expected full resolution to take time; specific loss figure not itemized publicly.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed; Maple Leaf publicly indicated it would not accede to criminal demands.
downtime: System outage began early November 2022 with recovery efforts extending over subsequent weeks while the company used workarounds to maintain supply.
data_impact: Not detailed publicly at scale; primarily an operational-disruption event.
summary: One of Canada's largest packaged-meats and food producers suffered a November 2022 outage attributed to Black Basta ransomware, causing a system disruption that affected operations and order fulfillment across its network; recorded in the ransomware.live sector dataset as a Black Basta victim.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::Dole Food Company
downtime: Production plants across North America were shut down, and all shipments were on hold.
data_impact: Employee information of an undisclosed number of employees was accessed.
summary: Dole Food Company confirmed a ransomware attack in February 2023 that accessed employee information. The attack led to the shutdown of production plants across North America and caused delays and shortages of products in stores.

id: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production::AGCO
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: AGCO, a leading US-based agricultural machinery producer, was hit by a ransomware attack that impacted some of its production facilities. The attack was attributed to the LockBit ransomware group, which has been involved in various cyberattacks recently.

financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; no company financial statement or disclosed cost found.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: Per HudsonRock infostealer telemetry referenced on the incident's ransomware.live page: 147 compromised employee accounts, 16 compromised user accounts, 106 third-party employee credentials, and 27 external attack-surface exposures identified. Underlying stolen data types/volume from the ransomware group's own leak were not detailed in available sources as of this writing (incident is very recent/
summary: AiLock, a double-extortion RaaS group active since March 2025, claimed Ferrovial - a global infrastructure and mobility operator involved in construction and design plus toll-road concessions - on its leak site. AiLock's model gives victims a 72-hour response window and up to five days to pay, threatening regulator notification and competitor disclosure if unpaid.

date: October 12, 2025 and April 8, 2026 (two separate claimed incidents)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed for either incident.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed for either incident.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed for either incident.
data_impact: Leak size described as 'unknown' in available secondary reporting for both incidents; no confirmed data-type breakdown found in public sources.
summary: Balfour Beatty, a leading UK-headquartered international infrastructure group delivering construction, engineering and support services across transportation, power, buildings and civil works in the UK, US and other markets, was claimed by two different ransomware groups within a six-month span: INC Ransom in October 2025 (targeting US operations) and CoinbaseCartel in April 2026 (UK).

country: United States (privately held, one of the world's largest engineering/construction/project-management firms, major US government contractor)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed by Bechtel; no company statement located.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: Specific data types/volume exfiltrated from Bechtel were not detailed in available sources; the broader Oracle EBS campaign is understood to have exposed enterprise financial, HR and procurement data (the standard EBS module set) at affected organizations generally.
summary: Bechtel was named by the Clop ransomware group as part of a large-scale extortion wave exploiting a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-61882) in Oracle E-Business Suite. Clop posted roughly 39 victim organizations across many industries within a 24-hour window in this campaign; Clop had earlier exfiltrated data via the Oracle EBS flaw in August 2025 and followed up with mass extortion emails in late September 2025 before publishing leak-site listings in November.

country: United Kingdom (major listed construction, property and infrastructure services company, LSE:KIE)
ransom: Not publicly disclosed; Clop threatened to release data absent negotiation.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: Per secondary reporting citing infostealer-derived telemetry on the incident record: 4 employees, 120 users, and 23 third-party employee credentials referenced as compromised/exposed; specific stolen-file categories from the Clop leak itself were not detailed in available sources.
summary: Kier Group, a leading UK construction, civil-engineering, property and infrastructure services company operating across defence, transportation, health, education and utilities, was claimed by Clop as part of the same Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2025-61882 mass-exploitation campaign that hit Bechtel days later.

country: United Kingdom / continental Europe operations of Kajima Corporation (Japan, one of the world's largest construction firms)
downtime: Not publicly disclosed/documented in available sources.
data_impact: Approximately 400 GB of data reported exfiltrated, including engineering documents, CAD designs and blueprints, financial and investment records, construction contracts and procurement documentation, internal communications, subcontractor lists and payment schedules, employee HR files/credentials, and project-management files.
summary: Qilin, one of the most prolific ransomware groups globally in 2025 (claiming roughly 800 victims across 50+ countries since January 2025, and dominant in Europe with 65 Q3-2025 victims per Cyble), claimed Kajima Europe, the European arm of major Japanese construction group Kajima Corporation, exfiltrating a large volume of corporate and project data.

country: United States (Fortune 500 global engineering, design and infrastructure-consulting firm)
financial_impact: Specific incident-response, remediation or credit-monitoring costs were not publicly disclosed; no stock-impact or insurance-payout figures found in public sources.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: Personal information of present and former AECOM employees was exposed, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and personal bank account and routing numbers, via compromise of the US payroll system; exact number of employees affected was not confirmed in available public sources.
summary: AECOM was compromised in a payroll-system hack attributed to the Pysa (Mespinoza) ransomware group's double-extortion operators; AECOM subsequently notified current and former employees that their personal data had been exposed and reported the incident to the California Attorney General's office. This is one of the better-documented incidents in the sector because it produced a formal breach notification rather than only a leak-site claim.

country: United States (one of the largest construction management firms in the US)
downtime: Not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: Specific data types/volume were not detailed in available public sources beyond the leak-site listing itself.
summary: Turner Construction Company was listed as a victim by the Everest ransomware group, a double-extortion (and increasingly pure data-extortion) operator active since December 2020 that has targeted government, healthcare, manufacturing and IT-services organizations across North America, Europe and Asia. Turner's inclusion illustrates the group's willingness to target top-tier construction management firms.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Donut extortion group has been confirmed to deploy ransomware in double-extortion attacks, targeting various enterprises including the multinational construction company Sando. The group uses customized ransomware that encrypts files and appends a specific extension, while also engaging in theatrics with their ransom notes and marketing strategies.

downtime: Knauf's global IT team shut down all IT systems to isolate the incident and is in the process of forensic investigation, incident response, and remediation.
data_impact: 20% of the files allegedly exfiltrated included email communication, user credentials, employee contact information, production documents, and ID scans.
summary: Knauf Group, a multinational building materials producer, was targeted by the Black Basta ransomware gang on June 29, 2022. The attack disrupted business operations, leading to a complete shutdown of IT systems while the company investigates and responds to the incident. Black Basta claimed responsibility and leaked 20% of the stolen files, indicating ongoing negotiations for a ransom payment.

id: Educational Services::PowerSchool (SIS vendor serving K-12 districts in the US, Canada and elsewhere)
victim: PowerSchool (SIS vendor serving K-12 districts in the US, Canada and elsewhere)
financial_impact: Total programme cost not publicly disclosed. PowerSchool offered two years of identity protection and credit monitoring to affected students and educators; class-action litigation followed. Individual district remediation and notification costs were not publicly itemised.
ransom: Approximately $2.85 million in bitcoin demanded and PAID by PowerSchool, per US Department of Justice court documents made public 20 May 2025. Amounts sought in the subsequent district-level extortion attempts were not publicly disclosed.
downtime: No mass encryption event - this was exfiltration-only extortion, so districts did not suffer the closure pattern typical of encryption attacks. Recovery centred on notification, credit monitoring, credential resets and multi-jurisdiction regulatory response, extending well beyond a year and reopening when re-extortion began in May 2025.
data_impact: The attacker claimed data on 62.4 million students and 9.5 million teachers across approximately 6,505 school districts in the US, Canada and other countries. Exposed fields included names, addresses, dates of birth, contact details, and for some individuals Social Security numbers and medical/grade information. Affected populations are overwhelmingly minors, whose identity exposure persists for d
summary: The defining edtech aggregation event. An attacker used compromised credentials to access PowerSchool's PowerSource support portal and exfiltrate student and teacher data from the hosted SIS environment. PowerSchool paid an extortion demand in exchange for a video purporting to show deletion of the only copy of the data. The deletion proved worthless: in May 2025 the same data was used to extort individual school districts directly in Canada and North Carolina, with attackers sending samples to schools. PowerSchool stated it did not believe this was a new intrusion because the samples matched the December theft. This is the clearest available demonstration that paying for a deletion promise transfers no risk downstream, and that a single vendor compromise generates thousands of correlated district-level losses.

date: 2026-05-01 (intrusion 29-30 April 2026; second breach within roughly two weeks)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed. Institutional costs spanned incident response, forensic review, portal remediation after defacement, and notification across thousands of schools.
ransom: Ransom PAID by Instructure under an agreement reached 11 May 2026; the amount was not publicly disclosed. Attackers reportedly returned the data and supplied 'shred logs' as claimed proof of destruction - the same unverifiable deletion assurance seen in the PowerSchool case.
downtime: Instructure took Canvas, Canvas Beta and Canvas Test offline on 7 May 2026 for investigation and restored service the following day; Canvas Data 2 and Canvas Beta had been in maintenance since 1 May. The Free-For-Teacher account programme was permanently shut down as a remediation measure. Roughly 330 institutions additionally had to remediate defaced login portals.
data_impact: ShinyHunters claimed 3.6TB covering 275 million users across approximately 9,000 institutions (reporting also cites 8,809 universities, education ministries and other bodies) - figures Instructure has not confirmed. Instructure confirmed exposure of names, email addresses, student ID numbers and some private messages between Canvas users, and stated there was no evidence that passwords, financial
summary: Described in reporting as the largest education-sector breach on record. ShinyHunters exploited Instructure's Free-For-Teacher (FFT) programme - which allowed educators to create Canvas accounts without institutional verification - to reach production data, then breached the platform a second time within about two weeks. After Instructure missed the initial 7 May negotiation deadline, the group escalated by defacing Canvas login portals at roughly 330 institutions and pivoting to direct school-by-school extortion with a final 12 May deadline. Instructure reached a payment agreement on 11 May, one day before the leak deadline. The incident is the purest example of LMS vendor concentration risk: Canvas is used by 41% of US higher education institutions, so a single platform intrusion simultaneously exposed thousands of otherwise unconnected insureds.

id: Educational Services::University of Hawai'i Cancer Center
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed. Costs included ransom payment, third-party forensic and recovery support, and notification plus remediation for up to 1.15 million individuals.
ransom: Ransom PAID - the centre worked with third-party cybersecurity experts to obtain a decryption tool and paid to prevent publication of the stolen data. The amount was not publicly disclosed.
downtime: Encrypted data was recovered using a decryption tool obtained through the payment. Specific outage duration was not publicly disclosed. Notification lagged roughly four months behind discovery, with the centre compiling names and addresses for study participants well after the August 2025 intrusion.
data_impact: Up to 1.15 million individuals affected (some reporting cites approximately 1.2 million). Exposed data included Social Security numbers and driver's licence numbers sourced from the Hawai'i State Department of Transportation, and City and County of Honolulu voter registration records from 1998. Much of the affected population were research study participants rather than students or employees.
summary: A university research-archive breach that illustrates how higher education accumulates liability for populations who were never students or staff. Attackers reached data from the Multiethnic Cohort (MEC) Study, a longitudinal epidemiological study established in 1993, plus files from three other diet-and-cancer studies. Compounding the event, the university did not notify affected study participants for roughly four months - a delay that drew specific public criticism and independent regulatory risk. Notably, the university PAID to prevent publication, making this one of the few education cases with a confirmed payment decision.

financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed. Costs included district-wide re-imaging of all student and staff devices, third-party forensic engagement, and three days of lost instruction across 34 schools.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed - the district declined to say how much was demanded, citing the ongoing investigation, and did not publicly confirm any payment.
downtime: All schools and activities closed for three days, from Monday 9 September through Wednesday 11 September 2024, reopening Thursday 12 September. Network systems remained disrupted into October 2024, when all student and staff devices had been re-imaged - roughly a month of degraded operation after classes resumed.
data_impact: The district confirmed that highly sensitive personal, financial and medical data was breached. The precise number of affected students and staff was not publicly disclosed in the reporting reviewed.
summary: The canonical K-12 operational-disruption case. Highline, a Washington state district of 34 schools serving roughly 17,500 students and 2,000 staff, detected the intrusion on a Saturday and immediately isolated critical systems - then closed every school and all activities for three days because core instructional and safety systems could not be trusted. It demonstrates the sector's defining characteristic for insurers: a school district has no degraded operating mode, so business interruption manifests as total closure of an essential public service, with statutory make-up obligations and knock-on effects to transport and meal programmes.

financial_impact: Approximately GBP 6-7 million in recovery costs, funded from roughly 40% of the library's financial reserves - about ten times the ransom demanded.
ransom: 20 bitcoin demanded, approximately GBP 596,000 at the time. NOT PAID - the library refused, and Rhysida published the data.
downtime: Services were severely disrupted for months. The main catalogue returned online on 15 January 2024 in read-only format, roughly two and a half months after the attack, with other services expected to remain unavailable for months beyond that. Recovery was complicated by legacy infrastructure and constrained funding, documented in the library's own transparency reporting and subsequent academic analysis.
data_impact: Approximately 600GB of material leaked publicly after refusal to pay, including internal documents and staff and user data. Full affected-individual counts were not publicly itemised in the reporting reviewed.
summary: The UK's national library, described as one of the worst cyber incidents in British history. Rhysida rendered almost all VMware ESXi servers unavailable, taking down the website, on-site services and Wi-Fi; the library remained physically open but could accept only cash payments. The institution refused to pay and Rhysida published the stolen material. The case is the reference point for catastrophic recovery severity in a public, non-commercial education/research body: the recovery cost dwarfed the ransom demand by an order of magnitude, and the library had to consume roughly 40% of its financial reserves - a funding mechanism with no analogue in the commercial sector and a key consideration for public-institution insureds.

date: 2023-06-05 (intrusion began 5 June 2023; detected 9 June; containment from 14 June)
ransom: Not publicly disclosed. No public confirmation of payment; the university worked with the ICO, NCSC and National Crime Agency.
downtime: Detected 9 June 2023 with containment beginning 14 June. Specific outage duration and full recovery timeline were not publicly disclosed; response ran in parallel with ICO and NCSC engagement.
data_impact: Around 250GB of data accessed. Included NHS records relating to 1.1 million patients across more than 200 hospitals, gathered for medical research - with NHS numbers and the first three letters of patients' postcodes among the fields, plus major-trauma and terrorist-attack victim treatment data. Separately, student and alumni data was leaked including names, contact details, gender, dates of birth
summary: The clearest illustration of research-data liability in higher education. Attackers reached a research archive holding NHS patient records gathered from more than 200 hospitals for medical research purposes - including major-trauma patient reports and treatment records for victims of terrorist attacks - alongside current student and alumni data. Attackers then emailed students and staff directly threatening to sell their data, a triple-extortion pressure tactic. The incident triggered questions in UK health and education policy about universities holding national-scale clinical datasets under research governance rather than clinical security controls.

id: Educational Services::Minneapolis Public Schools (Special School District No. 1)
victim: Minneapolis Public Schools (Special School District No. 1)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed. Costs included forensic investigation, restoration from backups, and notification plus credit monitoring for 105,617 individuals.
ransom: $1,000,000 demanded by Medusa with a 17 March 2023 deadline; the leak site also offered a $50,000-per-day deadline extension and listed the data for outright purchase at $1 million. NOT PAID - the district restored from internal backups and Medusa published the stolen files.
downtime: Widespread digital disruption following the 17 February 2023 encryption event; the district recovered encrypted data from internal backups rather than paying. Precise system-restoration duration was not publicly disclosed. Notification took seven months, completing in September 2023.
data_impact: 105,617 people notified as affected. Nearly 200,000 individual files containing sensitive student and educator information were released publicly, including student psychological and welfare records. Cybersecurity experts confirmed campus security maps and school security blueprints were among the leaked material - creating ongoing physical-safety risk to students.
summary: The reference case for extortion harm to minors and for notification failure. Medusa demanded $1 million with a 17 March deadline, posted the district on its leak site with a countdown, offered to sell the data to any buyer for $1 million, and offered the district the option to pay $50,000 per additional day of delay. The district refused and restored from internal backups - but Medusa then published the files. Analysts confirmed the leaked corpus included school security blueprints, a physical-safety exposure that cannot be remediated by notification or credit monitoring. The district publicly characterised the event as an 'encryption event' and did not notify the 105,617 affected individuals until September 2023, seven months later.

id: Educational Services::Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD)
date: 2022-09-03 (attack 3 September 2022; leak-site posting 30 September 2022; data published 2 October 2022)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed as a single figure. The district funded incident response, credit monitoring for affected individuals including contractors whose SSNs were exposed, and a subsequent security programme uplift.
ransom: Demand amount not publicly disclosed. NOT PAID - LAUSD publicly refused, stating public dollars are better spent on students than on criminals, and Vice Society published the data on its leak blog on 2 October 2022.
downtime: The attack disrupted district systems in early September 2022 at the start of the school year, though schools remained open. Threat actors had persistent access from 31 July to 3 September 2022 before detection - a dwell time of over a month. Full remediation timeline was not publicly disclosed.
data_impact: 500GB of data stolen and published. The trove included student psychological assessments, health information including COVID-19 test data, and prior conviction reports. LAUSD separately confirmed that contractors' Social Security numbers were among the stolen data. Passport data and other sensitive identifiers were also reported as potentially included.
summary: The attack that made K-12 ransomware a national policy issue in the US. Vice Society - the group that dominated education targeting in this period, ranking fourth all-time in the Education dataset with 63 victims - dwelled in the network of the second-largest US school district for over a month, from 31 July to 3 September 2022. LAUSD publicly refused to pay on the principle that 'dollars must be used to fund students and education' and that paying never guarantees full recovery, following FBI guidance. Vice Society published the full 500GB trove in retaliation. The leaked data's contents - student psychological assessments, health and COVID-19 test data, and prior conviction reports - established the template for how education extortion inflicts harm on minors specifically.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Interlock ransomware attack utilized a new malware strain called Slopoly, which was likely generated using AI tools. The attack involved data theft and extortion, with the threat group Hive0163 being responsible for the incident, which affected the Texas Tech University System.

downtime: The university's website remains offline, and technicians are working to restore systems from backups.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: La Sapienza University in Rome experienced a cyberattack that caused significant operational disruptions and led to the shutdown of its IT systems. Reports suggest that the attack is a ransomware incident linked to a pro-Russian group called Femwar02, which may have resulted in data encryption.

downtime: The company is working to restore its online services, a process that is reportedly in its final stages.
data_impact: Over 9.6 million accounts registered, corresponding to about 5.5 million people may have had their information exposed.
summary: Kyowon Group, a South Korean conglomerate, confirmed a ransomware attack that disrupted its operations and potentially exposed customer information. The attack occurred in January, affecting approximately 600 out of 800 servers, and the company is currently investigating the extent of the data breach while working to restore services.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: over 31,000 individuals affected, including sensitive data belonging to roughly 1,150 students, current and former employees, volunteers, and contractors
summary: Baltimore City Public Schools experienced a data breach in February 2025, affecting over 31,000 individuals. The breach involved unauthorized access to sensitive documents, including social security numbers and student data, and has been linked to the Cloak ransomware group. The school district is providing credit monitoring services to those impacted.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 517,487 individuals affected; personal, financial, and health data including driver's license or state IDs, social security numbers, account PINs, security codes, payment card information, passport information, taxpayer ID numbers, credentials, health insurance and medical information
summary: The Pennsylvania State Education Association (PSEA) experienced a data breach on July 6, 2024, affecting over 500,000 individuals. The Rhysida ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the breach, demanding a ransom of 20 BTC and threatening to leak the stolen data if not paid.

id: Educational Services::Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center
victim: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center
downtime: temporary disruption to some computer systems and applications
data_impact: 1,465,000 people; Full name, Date of birth, Physical address, Social Security number, Driver's license number, Government ID number, Financial account information, Health insurance information, Medical information, Billing/claims data, Diagnosis and treatment information
summary: The Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center suffered a cyberattack in September 2024, impacting the data of 1.4 million patients. The attack was claimed by the Interlock ransomware group, which leaked 2.1 million files totaling 2.6 TB of data on their extortion portal.

downtime: All systems are operational and none of their operations are disrupted.
data_impact: Approximately 247,000 students and 40,000 staff members potentially impacted; sensitive information may have been exposed.
summary: The Toronto District School Board (TDSB) experienced a ransomware attack on its software testing environment, prompting an investigation into potential exposure of personal information. TDSB has confirmed that all systems remain operational and that they are working with law enforcement and cybersecurity experts to assess the situation.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 800,000 individuals affected; Full or partial Social Security Number, Date of Birth, Bank account number(s), Federal income tax documents with Tax ID number, Driver's license number or identification card number
summary: The University System of Georgia was impacted by the Clop ransomware gang's MOVEit attacks, resulting in the exposure of sensitive data for 800,000 individuals. The organization began notifying affected individuals in April 2024 after determining that Clop had stolen sensitive files from its systems.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 27,000 individuals; personally identifiable information (PII) including date of birth, Social Security number, government ID, passport number, driver's license number, biometric data, health/medical information, email address with password, username with password, security questions and answers, digital signature, credit card information with security codes
summary: Stanford University experienced a ransomware attack that resulted in the theft of personal information belonging to 27,000 individuals. The attack was discovered on September 27, 2023, and was attributed to the Akira ransomware gang, which claimed to have stolen 430Gb of files from the university's systems and published the data on their dark web leak site.

downtime: several days of shutdowns
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: A ransomware attack on Truman State University caused several days of shutdowns and required the engagement of external security teams. The attack highlights the vulnerabilities educational institutions face, particularly regarding the protection of sensitive personal data.

id: Educational Services::Colorado Department of Higher Education
downtime: CDHE took steps to secure the network and have been working with third-party specialists to conduct a thorough investigation into this incident. CDHE also worked to restore systems and return to normal operations.
data_impact: The data stolen includes full names, social security numbers, dates of birth, addresses, proof of addresses (statements/bills), photocopies of government IDs, and for some, police reports or complaints regarding identity theft. The breach impacts students, past students, and teachers who attended public institutions in Colorado between 2004 and 2020.
summary: The Colorado Department of Higher Education disclosed a massive data breach following a ransomware attack on June 19, 2023. The attack compromised sensitive data affecting students, past students, and teachers, with the threat actors having access to the systems from June 11 to June 19, 2023. The stolen data includes personal information such as social security numbers and addresses, prompting the CDHE to offer identity theft monitoring to those impacted.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: On May 30th, 2023, the University of Waterloo experienced a ransomware attack targeting their Microsoft Exchange email service. As a result, the university mandated a mass password reset for staff, faculty, and students, affecting approximately 42,000 individuals. The reset process was scheduled to be completed by June 22nd, 2023, to mitigate potential security risks.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: approximately 28,000 people
summary: Hawai'i Community College admitted to paying a ransom to prevent the leaking of stolen data. The incident involved the data of approximately 28,000 individuals being at risk due to a ransomware attack.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Colorado State University confirmed that the Clop ransomware operation stole sensitive personal information of current and former students and employees during the MOVEit Transfer data-theft attacks. The breach impacts data from as far back as 2021, affecting personal identifiable information such as names, dates of birth, and social security numbers.

downtime: forced to take all networked systems offline
data_impact: data of not publicly disclosed number of people
summary: Des Moines Public Schools confirmed a ransomware attack that occurred on January 9, 2023. The BlackCat ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack, which involved data theft. The school district had to take all networked systems offline as a result of the incident.

downtime: All examinations were postponed; remediation and system restoration efforts are still underway.
data_impact: 1.2 TB of files, including admissions data from thousands of students, W-2 Tax Form for the University's President, and a document related to their insurance policy.
summary: The Avos ransomware gang hijacked Bluefield University's emergency alert system to threaten students and staff with the release of stolen personal data unless a ransom was paid. The incident led to the postponement of examinations and the release of some stolen data, including sensitive documents.

downtime: Several central services and critical systems went offline; extensions for assignment submissions were provided by academic staff.
data_impact: Student lists with personally identifiable information, financial details of research contractors, and more.
summary: The Medusa ransomware gang claimed a cyberattack on the Open University of Cyprus, disrupting operations and leading to the offline status of critical systems. The group demanded a ransom of $100,000 and published data samples to prove their claims, affecting sensitive information of students and contractors.

id: Educational Services::Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
downtime: The university is currently carrying out incident response activities and has blocked all communication networks. Some technical systems are gradually being restored, but the incident response is ongoing.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Technion - Israel Institute of Technology was hit by a ransomware attack from a group called DarkBit, which demanded a ransom of approximately $1.7 million. The attack was reportedly motivated by protests against tech layoffs and anti-Israel sentiments, and the university is actively responding to the incident while maintaining normal campus operations.

downtime: ongoing reconstruction of IT infrastructure
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Vice Society ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on the University of Duisburg-Essen in November 2022. The attack forced the university to reconstruct its IT infrastructure, a process that is still ongoing.

downtime: Campuses reopened on January 3, 2023, but system disruptions are expected to continue for some weeks.
data_impact: 10% of the data stolen includes HR files, email and letter communications, ID cards and documents, and financial and administrative documents.
summary: The Royal ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on the Queensland University of Technology, leaking data they allege was stolen during the breach. The university experienced significant service disruptions and shut down all IT systems to contain the attack, while also warning students and staff about potential risks.

id: Educational Services::Cincinnati State Technical and Community College
victim: Cincinnati State Technical and Community College
downtime: Restoration of on-campus networks and email, partial internet access, and classroom computers; however, voicemail, network printing, VPN access, and shared drives are unavailable, causing significant disruption.
data_impact: 10,000 students and 1,000 staff members affected; leaked documents contain personally identifiable information (PII).
summary: Vice Society ransomware claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on Cincinnati State Technical and Community College, leaking data allegedly stolen during the attack. The college informed its students and staff about the cybersecurity incident, indicating that online services and restoration to regular operations will take time.

id: Educational Services::Los Angeles Unified School District
downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 3,400 students and 2,200 employees affected
summary: Vice Society has been targeting the education sector with multiple ransomware strains, including a recent attack on the Los Angeles Unified School District. The group is known for exfiltrating data before encryption and threatening to leak it if ransom demands are not met. Microsoft has reported that Vice Society has been active in the U.S. education sector since at least July 2022, using various ransomware families and tactics.

downtime: Most centers still disconnected; just over 25% online as of the latest update.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) was hit by a ransomware attack attributed to Russian hackers over the weekend of July 16-17, 2023. Following the attack, the agency activated its cybersecurity protocols and isolated several research centers to control the situation, with most still offline as recovery efforts continue.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: approximately 4,500 employees' data including research, educational, and staff data, as well as salary payment information
summary: Maastricht University experienced a ransomware attack in December 2019, leading to the payment of a ransom to decrypt files. The attack was linked to the hacker group TA505, and the university later recovered the ransom amount through law enforcement efforts.

downtime: The university experienced an IT outage on June 20, 2022, and gradually restored its online services in the days that followed.
data_impact: 3,400 students and 2,200 employees; extensive list of documents allegedly stolen.
summary: The Vice Society ransomware gang claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on the Medical University of Innsbruck, causing significant IT service disruption and the alleged theft of data. Following the attack, the university reset all account passwords and began restoring services, while the gang leaked documents on their site, indicating a potential dead end in ransom negotiations.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: 495,448 students and 56,138 employees; personal information and assessment scores
summary: A ransomware attack on Battelle for Kids exposed the data of nearly 500,000 students and over 56,000 employees of the Chicago Public Schools. The breach involved personal information and assessment scores from the school years 2015-2019, with CPS learning about the breach four months after it occurred.

downtime: All systems required for recruitment, retention, and fundraising efforts were inoperable until fully restored in March 2022.
data_impact: no personal identifying information was exposed
summary: Lincoln College, a liberal-arts school in Illinois, announced its closure after 157 years due to the financial impact of a ransomware attack in December 2021. The attack disrupted admissions activities and hindered access to institutional data, leading to significant enrollment shortfalls and ultimately the decision to cease all academic activity by May 13, 2022.

downtime: shut down portions of their network while investigating the attack
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: Austin Peay State University suffered a ransomware attack, prompting the institution to shut down parts of its network for investigation. The attack was confirmed in late April 2022, and the university took measures to mitigate the impact on its operations.

financial_impact: No single official total disclosed by the company; national gasoline price spiked to a 6+ year high (~$3.04/gal). Ransom of $4.4M paid (see below). Widespread regional economic disruption from fuel shortages.
ransom: $4.4M paid (75 bitcoin) within hours, overseen by the FBI. On June 7, 2021 the DOJ announced seizure/recovery of 63.7 BTC, then worth ~$2.3M (lower than paid amount due to BTC price drop).
downtime: All pipeline operations halted May 7; systems and operations returned to normal by May 15 (~6-day shutdown). Decryptor tool from DarkSide was slow, so recovery largely relied on Colonial's own restoration.
data_impact: Attackers exfiltrated roughly 100GB of data prior to encryption (double-extortion); primary impact was operational/physical rather than a large PII breach.
summary: The largest refined-fuels pipeline in the US (Houston to the Southeast) was hit by DarkSide ransomware on its IT systems. Colonial proactively halted ALL pipeline operations to contain the attack. The 6-day shutdown interrupted fuel distribution to 17 states, triggering panic-buying, fuel shortages, and the highest average US gasoline price in over six years (~$3.04/gal by May 18). It is the defining cyber-physical energy ransomware case and prompted new TSA pipeline security directives.

financial_impact: ~$35M direct pretax cost reported in Q3 2024 results (filed late Oct 2024); ~$0.02 adjusted-EPS impact for the quarter from lost/delayed revenue during system unavailability.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed — Halliburton did not confirm whether a ransom was demanded, negotiated, or paid.
downtime: Precautionary shutdown of parts of IT infrastructure caused client-system disconnections and temporary inability to generate critical business documents; company described operational impact as limited and restored systems over subsequent weeks. Exact downtime not itemized.
data_impact: Data exfiltration confirmed; company stated information was taken from its systems. Specific record counts/data types not fully disclosed publicly.
summary: One of the world's largest oilfield-services companies detected unauthorized access to corporate IT on Aug 21, 2024 and precautionarily shut down certain applications, including production-planning and shipment-tracking systems used in customer delivery. RansomHub claimed the attack and listed the company on its leak site; Halliburton confirmed data was stolen. Disclosed via SEC Form 8-K (Aug 23) and 8-K/A.

financial_impact: Not publicly quantified as a single figure; disruption spanned 1,500+ retail sites over a weekend plus remediation costs (Suncor replaced employee laptops/computers as part of response).
ransom: Not publicly disclosed; Suncor characterized it as a 'cybersecurity incident' and did not confirm a ransom.
downtime: Payment-system disruptions began ~June 21 and were largely resolved over the following days; Suncor swapped out employee computers as a remediation measure, extending internal recovery activity.
data_impact: Unauthorized party accessed basic information of Petro-Points loyalty members; affected members and privacy regulators were notified. No large-scale financial-data theft publicly confirmed.
summary: A cybersecurity incident at Canadian integrated-energy giant Suncor disrupted its Petro-Canada retail subsidiary (1,500+ stations). Many stations went cash-only, unable to accept credit/debit or rewards; the Petro-Canada app, Petro-Points login, and car washes were unavailable at various sites. Illustrates downstream retail/payment-system exposure in vertically integrated energy firms.

id: Energy and Utilities::Encevo Group (Creos & Enovos, Luxembourg)
financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed as a dollar figure; operational impact limited to customer-portal outages (no supply interruption).
ransom: Ransom amount not publicly disclosed; ALPHV threatened to publish stolen data if unpaid.
downtime: Creos and Enovos customer portals were rendered non-operational following the July 22-23 intrusion; portals were restored over subsequent days/weeks while supply services remained running.
data_impact: ALPHV claimed exfiltration of 150GB+ across 180,000+ files, published on its leak site July 29 — contracts, agreements, ID copies, invoices, and emails; analyses found 2,270+ files containing plaintext credentials/passwords and 100,000+ documents marked confidential.
summary: Luxembourg's main energy supplier/distribution group — network operator Creos and supplier Enovos, under parent Encevo — was hit overnight July 22-23, 2022 by ALPHV/BlackCat (the DarkSide/Colonial lineage rebrand). Customer portals of Creos and Enovos were knocked offline, though electricity and gas supply and breakdown services continued uninterrupted. Demonstrates data-exfil-led extortion against European grid infrastructure.

financial_impact: Not publicly quantified; company emphasized transport operations were unaffected, limiting operational/financial disruption.
downtime: Business IT systems were isolated in response; SCADA/telecom and pipeline transport operations remained operational throughout (no OT downtime reported). IT recovery/remediation ongoing after Feb 2026 disclosure.
data_impact: Qilin alleged exfiltration of ~1TB including financial records, personnel data, and passport scans, and published sample images; Conpet confirmed data was stolen.
summary: Romania's national oil-pipeline transport operator detected a cyberattack on Feb 3, 2026 affecting its business IT infrastructure. Crucially, OT systems — SCADA and telecommunications — stayed fully functional and pipeline transport continued. Qilin claimed the attack and alleged theft of ~1TB of data. Root cause was an infostealer on an IT administrator's personal device; with valid WSUS credentials attackers abused Conpet's own update infrastructure to push a malicious 'fake update' delivering Qilin ransomware.

financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed at time of research.
ransom: Not publicly disclosed at time of research.
downtime: Not publicly disclosed at time of research.
data_impact: Claimed on ransomware.live leak-tracking; specifics of stolen data not independently confirmed at time of research.
summary: Ecopetrol, Colombia's state-controlled national oil company and one of Latin America's largest energy firms, was listed as a victim by the 'TheGentlemen' ransomware group on ransomware.live (attack date 2026-07-17). Included as a recent, geographically diverse, large-state-oil-company data point from the ransomware.live Energy sector feed. Detailed public reporting was not yet available at research time (July 19, 2026).

downtime: The incident caused disruptions and limitation of access to certain information systems, but manufacturing and field operations continued utilizing established downtime procedures.
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: On October 29, 2024, Newpark Resources, Inc. detected a ransomware incident where an unauthorized third party accessed its internal information systems. The company activated its cybersecurity response plan and is investigating the incident with external advisors.

downtime: not publicly disclosed
data_impact: not publicly disclosed
summary: The Gentlemen ransomware gang has been linked to the compromise of the Romanian energy provider Oltenia. They utilize a suite of EDR killers, including a tool named GentleKiller, to disable defenses during attacks, allowing for unimpeded data theft or encryption processes.
